This is also needed for any type of x-ray or CT scan.
These scans use a dye injected into your veins.
Be sure your caregivers know ahead of time that you are using metformin.
Tell your doctor if you have ever had:
kidney disease (your kidney function may need to be checked before you take metformin);
high ketone levels in your blood or urine;
heart disease, congestive heart failure;
liver disease or liver impairment
if you also use insulin, or other oral diabetes medications.
You may develop lactic acidosis, a dangerous build-up of lactic acid in your blood.
Lactic acidosis may be more likely if you have other medical conditions.
Lactic acidosis may be more likely if you have a severe infection.
Lactic acidosis may be more likely if you have chronic alcoholism.
Lactic acidosis may be more likely if you are 65 or older.
Ask your doctor about your risk.
Metformin immediate release tablets should not be given to a child younger than 10 years old.
Metformin should not be used for type 1 diabetes.
